Creating PLDM package is usually built on desktops/server class systems and not on BMC. In Nvidia we are using the upstream python tool for package building and works fine.

https://github.com/openbmc/pldm/blob/master/tools/fw-update/pldm_fwup_pkg_creator.py

Yes, you are 100% right.

But i need something that can be used in integration tests to check that the package is parsed correctly and the complete flow is working.

And i cannot pull in the pldm repository as a dependency here.

There is also the alternative which is to hardcode the pldm package
for each and every integration test.

But that does not scale well and lots of effort.

There was discussion to have PackageParser and maybe PackageBuilder (i did not discuss that yet) be part of libpldm as optional C++ bindings.

Which would make it more ergonomic to create and parse pldm fw packages.


Thanks for your input and taking a look at my patch 👍

This is all unit test code to create a dummy package with bunch of hardcoded package values. This isn't a tool to generate a package with input args passed in. Please move this inside the test code and update the description and other comments accordingly.

The component image is passed in as an argument.

Yes, some of the package values are hardcoded. Not all of them. It is a simplified library to test the flow. 

It is used in https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt/+/76100
as a tool for developers.

It is not a 'dummy package'. The package can contain a component which is not limited. There is currently one component which can be passed in.

I would like to use more of libpldm to 'properly' create the package using the encoding functions, but i'm afraid the 'encode_*' functions are not completely there yet.

https://github.com/openbmc/libpldm/blob/main/include/libpldm/firmware_update.h

So for now the package is generated in this way, which i hope to improve.

Maybe this patch can sit between the 'fw-update: common code' and 'fw-update: tests for common code' patches.

That way it will not be blocking the review and merge of the common code.

nvm, just saw that the package creation library is used by the tests for the package parser. 

So i can only re-order it before the 'fw update: pldm package parser tests',
or would need to hardcode the pldm packages used for these tests.
Please move this to test dir since you are hardcoding stuff for test purpose.
moved it 👍
In the latest code in repo, i have moved the existing code in bmc directory. As per our earlier discussion, please skip the fw-update directory and pull your code one level up.
Done
Please update the description mentioning this is a library to create test PLDM fw package.
Done. Missed that the first time around since your review comment was already marked as 'resolved'.

FYI: Currently, build_tests is defined in bmc/meson.build
Do u need to define build_tests locally or does it work as such?

From my experience, the meson variable definition is visible as soon as it is defined. 
Since ```subdir('bmc')``` has already completed.

I checked the meson docs but their explanation of variables does not include any information about their visibility to other meson files.
https://mesonbuild.com/Syntax.html
Using * and not &, any specific reason? Please keep it consistent through out code at other places as well.

C habits. 

```int&``` has the benefit that it is not nullable.
The downside is that at the call site, there is no indication that we are passing a reference. It looks like we are passing a value.

Adjusted it here.
I might be wrong, but i don't see you are using any APIs from this header? Is that code actually needed?

I am using the header.

```
76   create_pldm_firmware_device_identification_area_v1_0_0(...)
```

Why do you need this shared ptr? The caller already knows the size, so allocate a uninue_ptr there and pass to this func. It will automatically go out of scope when caller returns, no need to do this allocation here.

If possible do some error handling for allocation failure.

Yes, made it unique_ptr.

The caller should not need to know the size. The size
```
512 + component_image_size
```
is actually oversize and not spot-on. To calculate the size precisely ahead of time would require going through every function in a dry-run to calculate the size of each section. Since this is just test code and will not run often, just over-estimate the size.

Let me know if this needs to be spot on, we can calculate it but it will be extra code to do that.


> If possible do some error handling for allocation failure.

Why would we handle the allocation failure in a test case?

I assume it will throw std::bad_alloc, which is then not handled an crashes the program, resulting in test failure.
Which example?
removed that.
You can return std::optional<std::string> for better error handling.
Done
Log an error here?
Done
Please define the local helpers as static for clarity.
Done
Can you move the build_tests in this file and make sure the test still compiles in BMC dir.
Done
There is a C API also proposed @ https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/77429

Thanks for letting me know ❤️

Rajeev's patch looks much cleaner and less overhead, since it's all in C.

Let's see where it goes.

With the direction to move the package parsing logic to libpldm, phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt should only have changes to consume those APIs. So, unit testing of the APIs should move to the libpldm repo.

So phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt may not need this patch.

@alexander.hansen@9elements.com is adding this patch to automate the creation of test PLDM package for unit testing and its being added into test dir, so that should be fine.

About the packaging parsing logic, @alexander.hansen@9elements.com was also working on adding C++ bindings into libpldm via https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/77095. Until any of that goes in we are planning to have some version of this logic locally defined as in the next patch in this series. Once there is an API available in libpldm we will move to that.

@paligill@gmail.com There is a C version also being proposed for https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/77429. Please review if that meets all the requirements.

We should have bindings merged, and restrict pldm business logic to libpldm/pldm repos.

@rushtotom@gmail.com Sure i will review them. I have already mentioned above that we intent to use the APIs from libpldm, when they become ready. In the interim we will keep some logic locally in phosphor-bmc-code-mgmt and drop it in future and move to libpldm API when it gets merged.
